newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan '97 rubber consumption seen down 1.7% yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan '97 rubber consumption seen down 1.7% yr/yr.

text.p: Japanese rubber consumption is expected to total 1.419 million tonnes in 1997, down 1.7 percent from the record high levels of 1.444 tonnes reached in 1996, the Japan Rubber Manufacturers' Association said on Friday.
Good tyre production lifted rubber consumption last year.
Of the total, rubber consumption for tyres and inner tubes this year should fall by 1.9 percent to about 1.09 million tonnes, the industry body said.
The expected fall in rubber usage for tyres was attributable to an expected decline in tyres for new cars and exports, it said.
Rubber consumption for industrial products in 1997 is likely to be 275,000 tonnes, down 1.4 percent from 1996, while consumption for other rubber products should be flat at 59,000 tonnes, it said.
